general_background.title: Injection and precursor supply
general_background.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Phosphine-oxide coordination
general_background.summary: A phosphine oxide can interact with suitable precursor or surface sites through its oxygen donor. Competition among oxygen-donor ligands can change precursor coordination and the availability of surface sites.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
